1. THESE GENERAL NOTES PERTAIN TO WORK DESCRIBED ON ALL CONTRACT
DOCUMENTS.
2. THE WORK COMPRISES THE COMPLETED CONSTRUCTION REQUIRED BY THE
CONTRACT DOCUMENTS AND INCLUDES ALL LABOR NECESSARY TO PRODUCE SUCH
CONSTRUCTION, AND ALL MATERIALS AND EQUIPMENT INCORPORATED OR TO BE
INCORPORATED IN SUCH CONSTRUCTION.
3. SHOP DRAWINGS, PRODUCT DATA AND SAMPLES ARE A REQUIRED DELIVERABLE OF
THIS PROJECT, HOWEVER ARE NOT A PART OF THE CONTRACT DOCUMENTS. THE
PROJECT MANAGER WILL REVIEW THEM, BUT ONLY FOR CONFORMANCE WITH THE
DESIGN CONCEPT OF THE WORK AND WITH THE INFORMATION GIVEN IN THE
CONTRACT DOCUMENTS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL NOT BE RELIEVED OF
RESPONSIBILITY FOR ANY DEVIATION FROM THE REQUIREMENTS OF THE
CONTRACT DOCUMENTS BY THE PROJECT MANAGER'S REVIEW OF SHOP
DRAWINGS, PRODUCT DATA OR SAMPLES FOR SUCH PORTION OF THE WORK. FOR
LATEST INFORMATION ON DESIGN STANDARDS, SIGNAGE, AND SUBMITTALS GO TO
WWW.UNR.EDU/FACILITIES AND VIEW THE DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
DOCUMENT.
4. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL CAREFULLY STUDY AND COMPARE THE CONTRACT
DOCUMENTS AND SHALL AT ONCE REPORT TO THE ARCHITECT ANY ERROR,
INCONSISTENCY OR OMISSION HE MAY DISCOVER. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL
PERFORM NO PORTION OF THE WORK AT ANY TIME WITHOUT CONTRACT
DOCUMENTS OR, WHERE REQUIRED, APPROVED SHOP DRAWINGS, PRODUCT DATA
OR SAMPLES FOR SUCH PORTION OF THE WORK.
5. ALL WORK IS TO CONFORM WITH THE CONTRACT DOCUMENTS. DRAWINGS ARE NOT
TO BE SCALED FOR INFORMATION. IF UNABLE TO LOCATE DIMENSIONS FOR ANY
ITEM OF WORK, CONSULT WITH THE PROJECT MANAGER BEFORE PROCEEDING
WITH CONSTRUCTION.
6. IN THE EVENT CERTAIN FEATURES OF THE CONSTRUCTION ARE NOT FULLY SHOWN
ON THE CONTRACT DOCUMENTS, THEN THEIR CONSTRUCTION SHALL BE OF THE
SAME CHARACTER AS SIMILAR CONDITIONS THAT ARE SHOWN OR CALLED FOR AND
SHALL BE REVIEWED BY THE PROJECT MANAGER.
7. ALL WORK SHALL BE PERFORMED WITHIN STRICT CONFORMANCE TO THE MINIMUM
STANDARDS OF THE CURRENT EDITION OF THE INTERNATIONAL BUILDING CODE
AND ALL APPLICABLE NATIONAL, STATE AND LOCAL LAWS, REGULATIONS, AND
ORDINANCES.
8. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE GENERAL SAFETY OF
EMPLOYEES AND BUILDING OCCUPANTS DURING CONSTRUCTION, AND ALL WORK
SHALL CONFORM TO PERTINENT SAFETY REGULATIONS.
9. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL COORDINATE LOCATIONS OF ANY AND ALL MECHANICAL,
TELEPHONE, ELECTRICAL, LIGHTING AND PLUMBING INCLUDING: ALL PIPING,
DUCTWORK, AND CONDUIT. COORDINATE ALL REQUIRED CLEARANCES FOR
INSTALLATION AND MAINTENANCE OF THE ABOVE EQUIPMENT.
10. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL SUPERVISE AND DIRECT THE WORK. HE SHALL BE
RESPONSIBLE FOR ALL CONSTRUCTION MEANS, METHODS, TECHNIQUES,
SEQUENCES AND PROCEDURES AND FOR COORDINATING ALL PORTIONS OF THE
WORK UNDER CONTRACT.
11. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE ACTS AND OMISSIONS OF HIS
EMPLOYEES, SUBCONTRACTORS, AND THEIR AGENTS AND EMPLOYEES, AND OTHER
PERSONS PERFORMING ANY WORK UNDER A CONTRACT WITH THE CONTRACTOR.
12. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL COMPLETE THE WORK IN A CONTINUOUS AND DILIGENT
MANNER TO INSURE A TIMELY COMPLETION OF THE PROJECT.
13. UPON COMPLETION, CONTRACTOR SHALL PROVIDE OWNER WITH AS-BUILT
DRAWINGS.
14. THE CONTRACTOR AT ALL TIMES SHALL KEEP THE JOB SITE FREE FROM
ACCUMULATION OF WASTE MATERIALS OR RUBBISH CAUSED BY HIS OPERATION.
AT THE COMPLETION OF THE WORK HE SHALL REMOVE ALL WASTE MATERIALS AND
RUBBISH FROM THE PROJECT AS WELL AS ALL TOOLS, CONSTRUCTION EQUIPMENT,
MACHINERY AND SURPLUS MATERIALS.
15. UNLESS OTHERWISE PROVIDED IN THE CONTRACT DOCUMENTS, THE CONTRACTOR
SHALL PROVIDE AND PAY FOR ALL LABOR, MATERIALS, EQUIPMENT, TOOLS,
CONSTRUCTION EQUIPMENT, MACHINERY, UTILITIES, TRANSPORTATION AND OTHER
SERVICES NECESSARY FOR THE PROPER EXECUTION AND COMPLETION OF THE
WORK.
16. WHERE CONFLICTS OCCUR, COORDINATE THE LAYOUT AND EXACT LOCATION OF
ALL PARTITIONS, DOORS, TELEPHONES AND ELECTRICAL/COMMUNICATION OUTLETS
AND SWITCHES WITH THE PROJECT MANAGER IN THE FIELD BEFORE PROCEEDING
WITH CONSTRUCTION.
17. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL GUARANTEE ALL WORK AND MATERIALS TO BE FREE
FROM DEFECTS FOR A MINIMUM OF ONE YEAR FROM THE DATE OF FINAL
ACCEPTANCE, AND PROMPTLY REMEDY SUCH DEFECTS AND ANY SUBSEQUENT
DAMAGE CAUSED BY THE DEFECTS OR REPAIR THEREOF, AT NO EXPENSE TO THE
OWNER. GUARANTEE PERIODS OF GREATER THAN ONE YEAR MAY BE REQUIRED
AND CONTAINED WITHIN THE CONTRACT DOCUMENTS.
18. CONTRACTOR IS REQUESTED TO VISIT THE SITE AS PART OF THE PRE-BID SITE VISIT
TO COMPARE THE DRAWINGS AND SPECIFICATIONS WITH ANY WORK IN PLACE, AND
INFORM HIMSELF OF ALL CONDITIONS, INCLUDING THE WORK, IF ANY, BEING
PERFORMED. FAILURE TO VISIT THE SITE WILL IN NO WAY RELIEVE THE
CONTRACTOR FROM NECESSITY OF FURNISHING ANY MATERIALS OR PERFORMING
ANY WORK IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE DRAWINGS AND SPECIFICATIONS THAT MAY
BE REQUIRED TO COMPLETE THE WORK WITHOUT ADDITIONAL COST TO THE
OWNER.
19. EXISTING CONDITIONS INCLUDING MATERIAL SIZE, CONFIGURATIONS, AND
LOCATIONS AS SHOWN ON THE DRAWINGS MAY NOT BE AN EXACT ILLUSTRATION OF
EXISTING AS-BUILT CONDITIONS. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL INCLUDE IN HIS BID THE
COST OF FURNISHING, INSTALLING, MODIFYING, AND/OR NEW MATERIALS (MINOR IN
NATURE) REQUIRED FOR COMPLETE AND PROFESSIONAL INSTALLATION THAT MAY
BE REQUIRED BY MINOR VARIATIONS BETWEEN EXISTING CONDITIONS AS SHOWN,
AND ACTUAL AS-BUILT CONDITIONS.
20. ALL PENETRATIONS THROUGH FIRE RATED FLOORS / WALLS WILL BE FIRESTOPPED
WITH A UL APPROVED SYSTEM. THE FIRESTOPPING SYSTEM MUST BE FROM A
SINGLE MANUFACTURER.
21. MINIMUM OF 10 DAYS PRIOR NOTICE OF UTILITY SHUTDOWN IS REQUIRED.

1. ALL NEW CONSTRUCTION IS TO CONFORM TO PROVISIONS OF THE 2024 IBC
CODE AND LATEST UNR CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS AS ADOPTED AND
AMENDED BY UNR FACILITY SERVICES AND THE STATE OF NEVADA.
2. PATCH AND REPAIR ALL EXISTING CONSTRUCTION THAT IS TO REMAIN OR
HAS BEEN DAMAGED DURING CONSTRUCTION. ALL REPAIR WORK TO MATCH
EXISTING SURFACES.
3. ALL NEW WALL BOARD AND FRAMING SYSTEMS ARE TO ACHIEVE THE FIRE
RATING AS SPECIFIED.
4. FIELD VERIFY ALL EXISTING CONDITIONS AND DIMENSIONS PRIOR TO START
OF CONSTRUCTION.
5. VERIFY THAT THERE IS NO ASBESTOS PRESENT IN THE AREA OF
CONSTRUCTION. WORK WITH FACILITIES SERVICES AND ENVIRONMENTAL
HEALTH AND SAFETY FOR ASBESTOS ABATEMENT IF IT IS DETECTED.
6. CERTIFY THAT ALL NEW MATERIALS USED ARE NON-ASBESTOS CONTAINING.
7. ALL PENETRATIONS IN FLOOR/CEILING ASSEMBLIES ARE TO BE FIRED
STOPPED FOR MINIMUM OF 1-HOUR RATING.
8. ALL LAY-IN ACOUSTICAL PANELS AND DIRECT-HUNG ACOUSTICAL TILES
SHALL FOLLOW IBC CATEGORY D, E, F.

1. ALL WIRING SHALL BE IN EMT CONDUIT PER UNR DESIGN & CONSTRUCTION
STANDARDS.
2. MC CABLE IS NOT ALLOWED. SEE UNR STANDARDS FOR EXCEPTIONS.
3. EACH CONDUIT SHALL CONTAIN A CODE SIZED CU GROUND CONDUCTOR.
4. EACH SINGLE POLE CIRCUIT SHALL HAVE A DEDICATED NEUTRAL.
5. CONTRACTOR SHALL LABEL EACH OUTLET WITH CIRCUIT NUMBER AND
PANEL.
6. LIGHT FIXTURES SHALL BE SUPPORTED FROM BUILDING STRUCTURE WITH
2#12 STEEL WIRES CONNECTED AT OPPOSITE CORNERS.
7. RECEPTACLES SHALL NOT BE INSTALLED ABOVE CEILING.
8. THE CONTRACTOR SHALL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR THE PROTECTION OF ALL
EXISTING AND PROPOSED PIPING, UTILITIES, STRUCTURES, ADJACENT
STREETS AND IMPROVEMENTS DURING THE PERIOD OF CONSTRUCTION.
9. WHERE REMANUFACTURED OR PREFABRICATED ITEMS AND/OR MATERIALS
ARE TO BE INSTALLED, THE CONTRACTOR SHALL VERIFY ROUGH OR
FINISHED DIMENSIONS IN THE FIELD PRIOR TO PURCHASE OR FABRICATION.
10. BALANCE AIR FLOW SYSTEM WHEN COMPLETE.
11. EXISTING CONDUIT, CABLE, AND DUCTS TO BE SUPPORTED PER CODE.
